patterns: is a social media account a website
entries.answer: A website is a set of pages served from one place under one name, and the word has drifted well past that definition, so people say a website for a social media profile or an app that is not a website at all. What all of them share is being fetched over the network and identified by a URL. The word is also a compound, and whether someone says website or web site is a matter of house style rather than correctness.

entries.answer: A browser is the program that fetches pages and renders them, and the word names the software rather than the person using it, where the earlier sense of a browser as someone who looks around has almost died. It has to do three separate jobs: work out where to go, retrieve what is there, and display what came back. That the third is the hardest is not obvious, which is why rendering bugs outnumber network ones.

entries.answer: A download is a transfer of data from a remote machine to yours, and the word covers the transfer and the saved copy, so people say I downloaded it about the file and about the act. The inverse is an upload, and the asymmetry is not an accident, because downloading is what most people want and uploading is what a server does. A download that completes is a local file; a stream is the same data that never finishes being a file at all.

entries.answer: An upload sends data from your machine to a remote one, and it is the side almost nobody chooses, since files move outward only when a person is publishing or backing up. It is also the side that costs the network, because a home connection is built to deliver far more than it accepts. A large upload therefore fails where a large download would work, which is a property of the equipment rather than of the protocol.

patterns: is wifi the same as internet
entries.answer: Wifi is a family of standards for sending data over radio, and it is a trademark that was never enforced, so the word is now a generic name for wireless local networking. It does not mean the internet, which is the most common misunderstanding, since a network can carry local traffic with no route to anything else. The speeds quoted are theoretical, and real throughput depends on distance, walls, and what else in the room is transmitting.

patterns: how does a search engine rank
why does a page rank for a word it lacks
entries.answer: A search engine answers a query with a ranked list of pages, and the ranking is the whole product, since relevance is not something a page either has or lacks. The systems that produce those rankings have changed more than once, from counting words to following links between them to the learned systems in use now. That history explains why a page can rank well for a term it barely contains, which is the part that makes search marketing possible.
